builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
summary: This replaces rule-based or myopic (single-step uplift/response-model) next-best-action targeting with a Constrained MDP solved via linear programming, integrating causal off-policy correction of customer dynamics and yielding shadow prices for constraint trade-offs. The cost is not GPU compute but data and modeling effort: it requires logged customer-intervention data with adequate coverage, a defensible state representation (the paper uses RFM stages), causal estimation of transition dynamics, and LP machinery rather than standard supervised pipelines. Failure modes include misspecified causal dynamics that invalidate the off-policy correction, OPE that relies on a learned model rather than a randomized holdout (so the 19% figure may not transfer to live traffic), state aggregation that hides heterogeneity, and constraint shadow prices that mislead if the LP formulation omits real operational couplings.
rationale: The method is computationally cheap (no GPU or foundation model needed) and directly applicable to targeting problems, but its claimed gains rest on model-based evaluation with strong causal assumptions, so a pilot on the reader's own logged data with a randomized validation arm is warranted before production adoption.
technique: Causal constrained offline RL for next-best-action targeting

claims.statement: This replaces rule-based or myopic (single-step uplift/response-model) next-best-action targeting with a Constrained MDP solved via linear programming, integrating causal off-policy correction of customer dynamics and yielding shadow prices for constraint trade-offs. The cost is not GPU compute but data and modeling effort: it requires logged customer-intervention data with adequate coverage, a defensible state representation (the paper uses RFM stages), causal estimation of transition dynamics, and LP machinery rather than standard supervised pipelines. Failure modes include misspecified causal dynamics that invalidate the off-policy correction, OPE that relies on a learned model rather than a randomized holdout (so the 19% figure may not transfer to live traffic), state aggregation that hides heterogeneity, and constraint shadow prices that mislead if the LP formulation omits real operational couplings.

In a rideshare coupon case study with binary actions and RFM states, the optimized policy improves estimated customer LTV by 19% over the behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline, under model-based off-policy evaluation.
